motion_review: Viewed all 57 actual frames decoded from the nine final-previews GIFs as ordered nearest-neighbour 2x frame contacts; cross-checked the final atlas contact. No claim of real-time playback is used in place of frame inspection. All 57 frames across all nine standard states were inspected; per-frame concrete evidence is retained in state_reviews. Canonical base and both original reference-layout images inspected. Dark warm skin, ivory hair, white pupil-free eyes, pointed ears, ivory lightning torso marking, red sash, olive trousers, bare feet and broad sword with red guard/ring/chain remain recognizable across all 57 frames. Idle blink recovers; both directional gaits alternate extended and tucked limbs; waving returns arm to rest; jump rises above baseline and returns to its crouch; failure slumps then recovers; waiting, focused work and review have distinct attached-hand/head gestures. No missing frame, blade truncation, unexplained size pop or detached effect observed.

look_review.continuity: 000 raises the central head; 022.5/045/067.5 retain the upper-right family while pitch settles toward right 090. 112.5/135/157.5 bow toward lower-right, then 180 centers the bowed head. 202.5/225/247.5 turn the bowed head left, reaching level left 270. 292.5/315/337.5 raise the left profile, then 000 centers the raised head. Several adjacent intermediate cues are modest, but no opposite quadrant or reversal is visible. Both 157.5 to 180 and 337.5 to 000 continue the intended pitch family.
look_review.anchors: Torso/sash, sword-gripping arm, full down-left blade and both planted feet retain their orientation throughout; head, ears and attached hair follow the turn. No whole-body yaw, clipping or conspicuous registration jump observed.

minor_ambiguities.actual_ordered_review: The first downward head pitch retains a modest screen-right nose/cheek bias relative to the torso; it follows the right cardinal and leads the deeper rightward bow. The cue is weaker than 090 but does not point left.

The lowered head is more frontal than 090; the exposed face and nose retain a slight screen-right bias in the actual full cell and the descending right-side family. No opposite horizontal turn was observed.

The deeply bowed head approaches the central down pose, so its remaining rightward component is weak. The nose/face remains on the right side of its forehead/torso reference before centering at 180; this is a coherent approach to down.
The upward pitch is modest near the right cardinal. The chin remains raised with neck visible and then settles toward the more level 090 pose; the actual sequence does not bow downward early.

The first left-to-up intermediate has a modest upward pitch. Relative to 270, the chin begins rising and more neck is exposed; 315 and 337.5 strengthen that same pitch. No downward reversal was observed.

alpha_review.reason: All 16 alpha silhouettes and corresponding full-color final cells inspected. Alpha-zero enclosed suspects in alpha-topology.json occupy the chain/ring and negative space between held sword, wrist/arm and hip; narrow hair/arm silhouette openings follow visible exterior contours. The cyan-backed enlarged 000 and 180 cells confirm these openings follow actual chain/arm separation, while chest, abdomen, sash, trousers, face and broad steel blade remain opaque and continuous. No cross-body seam, horizontal band, severed limb or accidental blade hole observed. Enclosed pixel counts alone do not establish a defect.
